RagShortTexts: Siena stood as Florence's fierce Ghibelline rival, distinguished by its Piazza del Campo.

Variants.Content: Perched on three clay hills of southern Tuscany, the Commune of Siena was home to premier European merchant-banking syndicates like the Bonsignori. Fiercely Ghibelline, the city challenged Florentine hegemony, culminating in their crushing triumph at Montaperti in 1260.
Beneath the black-and-white balzana banner, citizen militias defended their republican charters with uncompromising civic fervor.
